newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Carpenter sees aerospace growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Carpenter sees aerospace growth.

text.p: An expected boom in U.S. aircraft manufacturing during the next five to six years should boost earnings at Carpenter Technology Corp, said Robert Cardy, its chairman, president and chief executive.
"I think (aerospace) is going to be a real growth segment for Carpenter," Cardy said in an interview with Reuters on Thursday. "It's a good segment."

The aerospace industry relies heavily on high-technology alloys for parts including engines. Cardy said his company will spend $100 million to $150 million during the next couple of years to expand its manufacturing capacity by 25 to 30 percent, with a focus on high-technology alloys.

Cardy also said he does not foresee any near-term price erosion on long products. Domestic producers of flat-rolled specialty steel products are struggling with weak pricing because of import pressure, but Cardy said prices for long-form products are stable.
"I don't see a downturn. I can see little bumps in the road. ...Unless something slows down, I don't think there's going to be a significant deterioration," he said.

Carpenter posted fiscal 1996 sales of $865.3 million, 14 percent higher than the prior year. Earnings grew to $3.51 per share from $2.81, with most of the growth coming from improved operating efficiency and a more favorable product mix.
Under Cardy's leadership, Carpenter in recent years has established manufacturing and distribution facilities in regions outside the United States to distinguish itself from its domestic competitors.

Carpenter also has acquired companies that produce materials other than alloys or specialty steel, such as ceramics, and has shifted its focus to providing more high-technology alloys rather than commodity steel products.

Despite those moves, Cardy said Carpenter's stock was undervalued. "It's a frustration," he said. "What else is there that we could do as a company to show people we're just not a steel company...and yet our multiples are right in there with companies that are making commodity steel products."
Carpenter shares were trading at 35-1/4 at midday Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange. "It should be no lower than 42," Cardy said.
"Our return on equity is up in the low 20s. We're growing; we've spread our wings outside the United States, and we're pursuing new technologies in other materials," he said.
